answer: By the ivory of the epoch the only identities still standing are the ones whose work held up. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. The shale holds work receipts rather than names, so the nadir of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, unlocked only after continuous uptime.
